deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page is headed 'P^α / Relationen zwischen benachbarten Functionen' (relations between contiguous functions) and, further down, 'Entwicklung in einen Kettenbruch' (expansion in a continued fraction). Riemann (i) derives the contiguous relations of his P-function from an Euler integral, and (ii) uses them to obtain Gauss's continued fraction for a ratio of two contiguous P-functions. The page is preparatory to his 1863 fragment 'Sullo svolgimento del quoziente di due serie ipergeometriche in frazione continua infinita'.

Notation. P = P(α β γ; α' β' γ'; x) has exponents α, α' at x=0, β, β' at x=∞ and γ, γ' at x=1. The 'base' function obeys α+α'+β+β'+γ+γ' = 0, written at the right of block 1. P(α+1) means the same expression with α raised by 1. Every once-shifted function therefore has exponent sum 1, which is Riemann's normalisation for a genuine P-function. The page later also uses multiply shifted functions such as P(α'−1, β+1, β'+1).

BLOCK 1 (first integral).
- Definition: P = e^{(α'+γ)πi} x^α (1−x)^γ ∫ s^{−α'−β−γ'} (1−s)^{−α'−β'−γ} (1−xs)^{−α−β−γ} ds.
- The image reads −α−β−γ in the last factor. This is also the only reading for which the stated relations hold.
- Write f for the integrand including the prefactors. Raising one exponent by 1 multiplies f by:
  - α'+1: −1/(s(1−s)) (the phase gives e^{πi} = −1);
  - β'+1: 1/(1−s);
  - γ'+1: 1/s;
  - α+1: x/(1−xs);
  - β+1: 1/(s(1−xs));
  - γ+1: −(1−x)/((1−s)(1−xs)).
- The four coefficient-free relations are then pointwise identities of integrands, valid for every integration path (my verification):
  - P(α'+1)+P(β'+1)+P(γ'+1) = 0;
  - P(α'+1)+P(β+1)−P(γ+1) = 0;
  - P(β'+1)+P(γ+1)−P(α+1) = 0;
  - P(γ'+1)+P(α+1)−P(β+1) = 0.
  These leave a 2-dimensional span for the six contiguous functions.
- Relations with coefficients come from ∫ d f = 0 (integration by parts; boundary terms vanish at the path ends). Set A = −α'−β−γ', B = −α'−β'−γ, C = −α−β−γ. Then f'/f = A/s − B/(1−s) − Cx/(1−xs).
- Decomposing this in the basis {1/(s(1−xs)), (1−x)/((1−s)(1−xs)), x/(1−xs)} gives A·P(β+1) + B·P(γ+1) − (A+B+C)·P(α+1) = 0.
- With A+B+C = −(α'+β+γ) = α+β'+γ' (using sum = 0), this is exactly the page's (α+β'+γ')P(α+1) + (α'+β+γ')P(β+1) + (α'+β'+γ)P(γ+1) = 0.
- The following lines are meant as the analogous relations for the other triples obtained by permuting the singular points.

BLOCK 2 (second integral, β and β' interchanged in the integrand).
- Definition: P = e^{(α'+γ)πi} x^α (1−x)^γ ∫ s^{−α'−β'−γ'} (1−s)^{−α'−β−γ} (1−xs)^{−α−β'−γ} ds.
- With exponent sum 1 this is x^α (1−x)^γ · const · F(α+β'+γ, α+β+γ; α−α'+1; x) for the path 0→1.
- Branches by path, as listed on the page: P^α = ∫_0^1 and P^{α'} = ∫_{1/x}^∞; the others are ∫_0^∞, ∫_0^{1/x}, ∫_1^∞ etc.
- The point of the list: the contiguous relations and the continued-fraction recursion hold for every branch. Which branch the continued fraction actually converges to is the question of the 1863 fragment.
- My computation of the once-shifted functions, with base sum 0, a = α+β'+γ, b = α+β+γ, c = α−α':
  - P(α'+1) ∝ −x^α(1−x)^γ Γ(b)Γ(c−b)/Γ(c) · F(a,b;c;x);
  - P(β'+1) ∝ x^α(1−x)^γ Γ(b)Γ(c−b+1)/Γ(c+1) · F(a+1,b;c+1;x);
  - P(α+1) ∝ x^{α+1}(1−x)^γ Γ(b+1)Γ(c−b+1)/Γ(c+2) · F(a+1,b+1;c+2;x).
  Here c−b = −(α'+β+γ) and c−a = α+β+γ'.
- Hence (α'+β+γ)/(α−α') · P(α'+1)/P(β'+1) = F(a,b;c)/F(a+1,b;c+1). This is the left side Riemann writes.
- Integration by parts with the block-2 integrand gives (my derivation) (α'+β+γ)P(α'+1) + (α+β+γ')P(α+1) − (α−α')P(β'+1) = 0.
- Therefore (α'+β+γ)/(α−α') · P(α'+1)/P(β'+1) = 1 − (α+β+γ')/(α−α') · P(α+1)/P(β'+1). In hypergeometric terms this is Gauss's relation F(a,b;c) = F(a+1,b;c+1) − b(c−a)/(c(c+1)) · x · F(a+1,b+1;c+2).
- Iteration: the new ratio P(β'+1)/P(α+1) is again a ratio of the same type, with parameters shifted (α→α+1, α'→α'−1, β→β−1 etc.). The page expresses this with multi-index P's and factors x, e.g. x·P(α'−1, β+1, β'+1).
- Iterating yields Gauss's continued fraction. Riemann writes it as:
  (α'+β+γ)/(α−α') · P(α'+1)/P(β'+1) = 1 + [(α+β+γ')/(α−α') · (α'+β'+γ')/(α−α'+1)] x / (1 + [(α+β'+γ+1)/(α−α'+1) · (α'+β+γ−1)/(α−α'+2)] x / (1 + ...)).
- Since α'+β'+γ' = −(α+β+γ) and α'+β+γ−1 = −(α+β'+γ'+1), this equals 1 − k1 x/(1 − k2 x/(1 − ...)) with:
  - k1 = (α+β+γ)(α+β+γ')/((α−α')(α−α'+1)) = b(c−a)/(c(c+1));
  - k2 = (α+β'+γ+1)(α+β'+γ'+1)/((α−α'+1)(α−α'+2)) = (a+1)(c−b+1)/((c+1)(c+2)).
  These are exactly Gauss's coefficients.
- The earlier draft of the continued fraction (upper right of block 2) has '+' signs, i.e. the wrong sign.
errors: Block 1 integrand: if the last factor is read as (1−xs)^{−α−β'−γ} (as in the machine transcription), none of the four stated three-term relations holds. With (1−xs)^{−α−β−γ}, which is what the image appears to show, all of them hold exactly.

The line '(α'+β+γ)P(α'+1)+(α'+β'+γ)P(β'+1)−(α'+β+γ')P(γ'+1)=0', as transcribed, cannot be right. Together with P(α'+1)+P(β'+1)+P(γ'+1)=0 in a 2-dimensional span it would force proportional coefficients. Either it is misread (probably different shifted exponents) or it is a slip.

Block 2: the coefficient-free relations as transcribed (copied over from block 1) do not fit the block-2 integrand. For that integrand the correct ones are P(α'+1)+P(β+1)+P(γ'+1)=0, P(α'+1)+P(β'+1)−P(γ+1)=0, P(β+1)+P(γ+1)−P(α+1)=0 and P(γ'+1)+P(α+1)−P(β'+1)=0. The shorthand lines '(α)=(β')+(γ')' etc. look like an unfinished attempt to redo this bookkeeping.
Sign slip: '(α'+β+γ)P(α'+1)+(α+β+γ')P(α+1)+(α−α')P(β'+1)=0' should have −(α−α')P(β'+1). Correspondingly '... = 1 + (α+β+γ')/(α−α') P(α+1)/P(β'+1)' should read '1 −'.

The first continued-fraction draft has '+' where Gauss's continued fraction has '−' (k1 = (α+β+γ)(α+β+γ')/(c(c+1)) enters with a minus sign). Its second partial numerator also seems to have β for β' (it should be α+β'+γ+1). The later version, written with α'+β'+γ' and α'+β+γ−1, has the correct signs.
'(α'−α−1)' in a lower line is presumably (α−α'+1) or a sign variant. The lower part of the page is exploratory, with several cancelled lines.

results.what: Contiguous ('benachbarte') relations of the Riemann P-function derived from an Euler-type integral: coefficient-free three-term relations as pointwise integrand identities, and coefficient relations via integration by parts, valid for all branches (all integration paths)
results.modern_name: Contiguous relations of the hypergeometric function / Riemann P-symbol (Gauss contiguous relations in Riemann's symmetric form)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1812) for the contiguous relations; Riemann (1857, 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen') for the P-function form

results.what: Gauss continued fraction for the ratio of contiguous P-functions, (α'+β+γ)/(α−α')·P(α'+1)/P(β'+1) = 1 − k1 x/(1 − k2 x/(1 − ...)), with integration paths P^α=∫_0^1, P^{α'}=∫_{1/x}^∞ etc. specifying the branches
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1812); Riemann studied its convergence in the 1863 fragment 'Sullo svolgimento del quoziente di due serie ipergeometriche in frazione continua infinita' (published in his Werke)

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes for known material. The P-function contiguous relations appear in Riemann's 1857 paper, and his study of Gauss's continued fraction for ratios of contiguous hypergeometric functions is in the published 1863 Nachlass fragment. The neat convention (base exponent sum 0, so each once-shifted P is a genuine P-function) and the branch-by-path list are pleasant details but not new results.

Block-1 relation list ends '... P(γ'+1)+P(α+1)−P(β+1)=0', written across the right margin.
First continued fraction, second partial numerator: probably 'α+β'+γ+1' (the image shows a prime on β), not 'α+β+γ+1'.
